1. Quasi-Riemann hypothesis: This gives much stronger guarantees on how irregularly primes can be distributed, by restricting where zeros of the zeta function and related functions can occur. That said, this establishes a boundary at 7/8. the full Riemann hypothesis requires 1/2 and remains unsolved.
2. Unique Games Conjecture: New limits on how well polynomial-time algorithms can approximate optimization problems like Max-Cut and Vertex Cover. The caveat on this one is that interpreting it still assumes P /neq NP. Doesn't resolve P = NP.

The release is a volume: hundreds of manuscripts, a subset with Lean checks, most attempTED problems still failed, and the zeta paper was the one a person ediTED. Family 003 on disk is not a classical zero-free argument on one page. It is a challenge stub ending in sorry, a one-line call, and a certificate assembly across a large tree. A text scan is not a kernel. This desk has no green log and no red log.
Swinging a lot at the wall is a fair description of the catalogue. It is not yet a description of a failed theorem. A green comparator would certify the staTED nonvanishing past (7/8), and that would still leave the band of width (3/4). A red log, a hidden sorry, or an axiom outside propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice kills the stamp. Until one of those arrives, the claim is incomplete, not occupied.

She won the World Cup. Then she gave up the captaincy. 
 Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down as India's women's captain across all formats, and she did it after leading India to back-to-back Asian Games golds. 
Think about what she has done. After Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni, she is only the third captain to win the ODI World Cup for India. 
Many people felt this moment was coming. But most captains are pushed out after a loss. She chose to step aside after a win, peacefully. She will keep playing, and she said the journey continues. 
What I'll remember most is her aura on the field. That charm between the matches. And the moment she won the World Cup and jumped onto her father like a little girl. 
A captain who lifted the trophy and was still just her father's daughter. 
This girl is amazing. Thank you, Captain. 
 What is your favourite Harmanpreet moment? Tell me in the comments.

World Bank Just Upgraded India. Again.
FY27 GDP growth forecast: 7.1% (up from 6.6%).
FY28: 7.2%.
India already grew 7.8% in FY26.
Why this matters:
Fastest-growing major economy in the world – even as global headwinds persist.
7.1% vs 6.9% South Asia average; 
Growth backed by domestic demand + strong exports, not just base effects.
Structural reforms doing the heavy lifting: Labour Code, GST, tariff rationalisation, IBC, infra push 
Medium-term outlook: ~7.1% average through FY28–29, with narrowing CAD and easing inflation.
Risks?
Yes – higher crude, El Niño-led food inflation, and possible market corrections.
But the World Bank’s view is clear: these are near-term

It was a seemingly innocuous email, sent on a Wednesday morning in January 2017, that started everything.
Arriving in the inbox of a senior official at Manchester City, it appeared to have been sent by an employee from European football’s governing body, UEFA, and contained a link to a financial compliance report.
The City official clicked the download button. That was all it took.
It was not a genuine email from UEFA but a successful phishing attempt by Portuguese hacker and activist Rui Pinto. City’s servers were breached, allowing Pinto to retrieve thousands of emails and documents from the club’s systems.
This week, almost 10 years on from Pinto’s first email, the Premier League announced that an independent panel had found City guilty of all but one of the charges against them, as The Athletic first revealed last Friday.
